learning_objectives: Explain part-whole meaning using simple language and an example.

lessons.objective: Learner can understand, explain and apply part-whole meaning.
teaching_sequence: Begin with a concrete or familiar situation.
Name the mathematical idea and connect it to prior knowledge.
Model a complete worked example with every step explained.
Move from representation to symbols and then to a new problem.
Ask the learner to explain the method without copying.
lessons.checkpoint: Explain part-whole meaning without notes and solve a new example.

items.question: Which approach best helps you understand part-whole meaning?
options: Identify what is known, represent it clearly, choose a valid method, and check the result.
Choose an operation before reading the problem.
Copy a worked answer.
Guess and stop.
items.explanation: Understanding the situation, choosing a method and checking the result makes mathematical reasoning reliable.

items.question: Explain part-whole meaning as if you were teaching it to someone learning from the basics.

flashcards.back: Define part-whole meaning, give an example, and explain why it matters.
Define equivalent fractions, give an example, and explain why it matters.
Define comparison, give an example, and explain why it matters.

interactive_activities.title: Explore part-whole meaning
interactive_activities.instructions: Use a safe, age-appropriate task specifically focused on part-whole meaning. Record what you notice, explain it, and state what you learned.

interactive_activities.title: Use it in a new situation
interactive_activities.instructions: Create a new situation where equivalent fractions is useful and explain your reasoning.

interactive_activities.title: Teach it back
interactive_activities.instructions: Teach operations with fractions to a beginner in 3–5 clear steps.
